Threat model\n968\t\n969\tThe README claims \"provably no exfiltration\" and \"auditable once and trusted thereafter\".\n970\tThat claim needs backing. In scope for v1:\n971\t\n972\t| # | Threat | Stance | Test |\n973\t|---|---|---|---|\n974\t| **T1** | **Crafted optical stream — resource exhaustion.** Beacon-declared `originalSize` and `payloadLen` (281 TB each), `blockCount` (16.7 M) and `L` are attacker-controlled and size allocations. | **Mitigated.** Bounds-check every beacon field before use: `L` ∈ [1, 4096], `K` ≤ locally benchmarked max (D26), `blockCount` ≤ 16.7 M, `originalSize` ≤ available quota, `payloadLen` ≤ available quota. Reject with `E-META-BOUNDS`. Never allocate from a declared size. | A10 + fuzz beacon fields |\n975\t| **T2** | **Path traversal / hostile filename.** `filename` is attacker-supplied and reaches a save dialog. | **Mitigated.** Strip path separators, control bytes and leading dots; cap length; never pass through unsanitised. | unit: filenames with `../`, NUL, control bytes |\n976\t| **T3** | **Decompression bomb.** The receiver decompresses attacker-supplied data. | **Mitigated.** Enforce a max expansion ratio (100:1) and an absolute cap = declared `originalSize`; abort with `E-DECOMPRESS` on overrun. | unit: 1 GB-expanding zip bomb → `E-DECOMPRESS` |\n977\t| **T4a** | **Sender-side plaintext residue.** D8 writes a *decompressed-equivalent* copy of the user's file to OPFS as staging. For the flagship use case (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds) this is real exposure. | **Mitigated.** Wipe staging on completion, on cancel, and on startup-reap (E11). Document that OPFS is not encrypted at rest and the OS/browser may retain it. | integration: assert sender OPFS empty after complete/cancel/reap |\n978\t| **T4b** | **Receiver-side plaintext residue.** The receiver stages the complete decoded file in OPFS. The output **is** the deliverable — it cannot be deleted immediately. For sensitive files (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds) indefinite storage is exposure. | **Mitigated.** Implement a deletion lifecycle: (1) delete after successful `share()`/`save()`; (2) reap orphaned outputs on startup; (3) warn before keeping partial artefacts (E10, E15); (4) provide a user-visible delete control. Document that OPFS is not encrypted at rest. | integration: assert receiver OPFS empty after successful save; reap deletes orphans; UI has delete control; warning shown for partial artefacts |\n979\t| **T5** | **Supply chain.** The security claim depends on the bundle being what was audited. | **Partially mitigated.** `bf-13h` covers the output half (version footer + published hash). The input half — pinned dependency versions, WASM integrity, no post-install scripts — is a Phase 0 requirement (§14.5). | G3: lockfile diff + SRI check in CI |\n980\t| **T6** | **Shoulder-surfing / filming.** The optical channel is uniquely exposed: anyone with a camera in the room captures the same stream. | **Accepted for v1, consciously.** concept.md scopes encryption as a non-goal; §19 Q10 keeps it live. The app MUST NOT claim confidentiality it does not provide — the UI should say the transmission is visible to anyone who can see the screen. | none — accepted, not mitigated |\n981\t| **T7** | **No telemetry, by construction.** | **Committed.** The app makes **zero** network requests after load. Enforced by CI (§14.4) and by A8. This is a stronger and more checkable claim than a privacy policy. | §14.4 network assertion + A8 |\n982\t\n983\t**Out of scope for v1, stated:** authenticating the *sender* (no PKI, no trust anchor); a\n984\tmalicious *receiver* (it only gets what it is shown); side-channels other than the optical\n985\tone; physical device compromise.\n986\t\n987\t---\n988\t\n989\t## 13. Performance budgets and benchmark contract\n990\t\n991\t### 13.1 Budgets — committed, not forecast\n992\t\n993\t§15's table is *expectation*. These are the numbers the build is held to.\n994\t\n995\t**Throughput basis.** All throughput budgets are **user-visible file bytes per second** after:\n996\t- Fountain coding overhead (+12% p99 at K=768 with D25's cap)\n997\t- Erasure loss (20–30% assumed band per D18c)\n998\t- Dwell overhead (60% standing overhead per §8.1)\n999\t\n1000\tThe gross wire rate at the R2 nominal rung (v16-L, 2 packets/tile, 15 tiles, 15 fps) is\n1001\t**112.5 KB/s payload** (7.5 KB/frame × 15 fps). After fountain (+12%) and 30% erasure,\n1002\tnet goodput is **~70 KB/s** — well above the 20 KB/s budget.\n1003\t\n1004\t| Budget | Value | Gate |\n1005\t|---|---|---|\n1006\t| Throughput, A1 reference setup | **≥ 20 KB/s** sustained | Phase 3 |\n1007\t| Throughput, A3 phone→phone | **≥ 3 KB/s** sustained | Phase 3; miss triggers §18 R4 |\n1008\t| Block-layer working set | **≤ 1 MB**, any file size (I6a) | Phase 1 |\n1009\t| Whole-receiver peak | **≤ 64 MB**, ≤ 4 in-flight `VideoFrame`s (I6b) | Phase 3 |\n1010\t| GE sustained XOR need | **≤ 200 MB/s** at the fastest supported stage (modelled 114.6 MB/s, 1.74× margin) — **measured 3,260 MB/s desktop / ~815 MB/s est. phone; the budget was ~16× pessimistic.** R1 provisionally closed, pending an on-device run *while thermally throttled* | Phase 1 + G7 |\n1011\t| Per-camera-frame decode | **≤ 60 ms** p99 (leaves headroom at 15 fps) — **measured 67–69 ms p50 full-frame, 194 ms at 4K, 6.6 ms with a tight ROI. p50 already exceeds the p99 budget**; the fixes (worker pool §6.2, tight ROI §6.4) are unimplemented, so this is violated by the instrument, not yet by the design | Phase 3 |\n1012\t| Encode + render per frame | **≤ 20 ms** p99 — **measured ~150 ms** (6.7 fps against 12 requested) on a 2015 laptop with D4's pinned mask unimplemented | Phase 3 |\n1013\t| Time-to-first-packet after aim | **≤ 3 s** p50 | Phase 5 |\n1014\t| Reception overhead vs K | **≤ +5%** mean, **≤ +12%** p99 (measured: +2.97% / +4.2%) | Phase 1, `sim/` |\n1015\t| **Sustained operation duration** | **≥ 20 min** sustained throughput within **30% of initial rate** on target phone (Pixel 6-class) without active cooling. This is the **minimum viable duration** before R11's thermal throttling mitigation (duty-cycle reduction) must engage. The system is not required to avoid throttling indefinitely—only to (a) sustain long enough for practical use and (b) detect and surface throttling when it occurs (E17b, D27). | Phase 3; validated by T-long-run |\n1016\t| **Warn threshold** (D23) | estimated duration **> 30 min** → explicit confirm | Phase 4 |\n1017\t| **Refuse threshold** (D23) | estimated duration **> 24 h**, or quota insufficient → refuse with an override | Phase 4 |\n1018\t\n1019\t### 13.2 Benchmark denominator — the contract\n1020\t\n1021\tEvery throughput number in this repo MUST state all of these, or it is not a measurement:\n1022\t\n1023\t| Parameter | Reference value |\n1024\t|---|---|\n1025\t| **Unit** | **User-visible file bytes per second.** Not wire bytes. With compression these differ 3–10×. |\n1026\t| Sender | 1080p display, 50%+ brightness, DC-balanced frames |\n1027\t| Receiver | Mid-range Android (Pixel-6-class), rear camera |\n1028\t| Distance | 30 cm (laptop→phone), 15 cm (phone→phone) |\n1029\t| Mounting | Tripod for budget figures; handheld reported separately, never mixed |\n1030\t| Lighting | ~300 lux, no direct glare |\n1031\t| File | 1 MB of random bytes (incompressible) unless stated |\n1032\t| Duration | ≥ 60 s sustained; startup excluded |\n1033\t| Trials | ≥ 5; report median and p99, never the best run |\n1034\t\n1035\t**§15's comparison table mixes measurement regimes** — PixNet's 12 Mb/s used a 30\" LCD and\n1036\ta 24 MP DSLR. Such figures MUST be labelled with their regime and never compared directly\n1037\tto handheld numbers.\n1038\t\n1039\t---\n1040\t\n1041\t## 14. Testing strategy and quality gates\n1042\t\n1043\t### 14.1 Tiers\n1044\t\n1045\t| Tier | What | Runs |\n1046\t|---|---|---|\n1047\t| **T-unit** | Codec internals, header parse, CRC, bitmap, repair-code round-trip | Every commit |\n1048\t| **T-property** | Random files × random loss patterns → byte-exact; overhead within simulation bounds | Every commit |\n1049\t| **T-stub-camera** | `getUserMedia` stubbed with `canvas.captureStream(0)` + `requestFrame()`. No flags, frame-exact, deterministic | Every commit |\n1050\t| **T-degradation** | Synthetic blur / rotation / keystone / glare / rolling-shutter tearing applied to rendered frames. **Assert decode *rates*, not booleans** | Nightly |\n1051\t| **T-real-capture** | Frames → Y4M → Chromium fake camera. Proven in research (byte-exact, including late-join at 700 ms) | Nightly |\n1052\t| **T-scale** | Synthetic 4 GB stream at the block layer; assert flat memory across 21,800 blocks | Nightly |\n1053\t| **T-long-run** | **20–30 minute sustained run** on real devices to validate thermal behavior (R11), duty-cycle economics (D27), and sustained throughput. Tracks fps decline, decode rate, and effective goodput over time. **This is the ONLY tier that can measure R11 and D27** — the 60 s floor in §13.2 structurally excludes thermal phenomena. | Weekly (or per thermal-related change) |\n1054\t| **T-physical-rig** | Two real devices, fixed mounting, the §13.2 denominator. **This is the acceptance gate for §13.1 throughput** — nothing else can measure it | Per release |\n1055\t| **T-manual-iOS** | Full pass on a real iPhone. **Not CI-testable at any price** — WebKit cannot fake a camera, the Simulator has none | Per release |\n1056\t\n1057\t> **Trap, already paid for:** `--use-fake-device-for-media-capture` **does not exist**. It\n1058\t> is `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream`, and the file flag requires it.\n1059\t\n1060\t### 14.2 Binary-safety testing\n1061\t\n1062\t**MUST use real compressed payloads at several lengths — never ASCII.** Corruption in the\n1063\trejected libraries was both *content*- and *length*-dependent: the same generator\n1064\tround-tripped at 600 bytes and corrupted at 256. Edge case catalog\n\n| # | Case | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| E1 | **Zero-byte file** | Reject at selection with a clear message. `K = 0` is undefined. |\n| E2 | **File smaller than one fragment** (< 256 B) | Pad to one fragment; `K = 1`; the fountain code degenerates to repetition, which is correct. Research specifies a `K < 8` guard — adopt it: below 8 fragments, send plain repetition, no LT. **Repetition is derived per-block** (not signalled): both encoder and decoder derive `repetition = (k < MIN_LT_K)` from the block's K using the shared per-block derivation E3a already mandates. A session-wide flag would force repetition on all 21,845 blocks or none; per-block derivation allows the last block (K=1-7) to use repetition while all other blocks (K=768) use LT. |\n| E3a | **The last block is short** — its K is `ceil(lastLen / L)`, not 768. Both sides derive K per block, and D7's PRNG is seeded with it. A mismatch produces wrong index sets, so the block never decodes and nothing says why. | Derive per-block K from `(blockIndex, blockSize, payloadLen)` in **one shared function** used by both encoder and decoder; conformance vector covers the last block explicitly. The beacon's `payloadLen` field (§7.2) is critical — without it, the receiver cannot compute the last block's actual length (`lastLen = payloadLen − (blockCount − 1) × blockSize`), leading to PRNG index mismatch and silent decode failure. |\n| E3b | **`blockCount == 1`** | Normal path; no special case, but tested explicitly since off-by-one in block iteration is likely. |\n| E4 | **Incompressible input where deflate expands it** | D8 samples first; if the sample ratio > 0.92, skip compression. If compression still expands, discard the staging file and send raw. |\n| E5 | **Source file changes mid-transfer** | A 10-hour read of a live `File` handle is the *normal* case. Re-check `file.size` and `lastModified` before each block read; on mismatch abort with `E-SOURCE-CHANGED`. Emitting blocks from two versions would produce a file that passes per-block hashes and fails the whole-file hash after hours. |\n| E6 | **Duplicate packet arrives** | GE reduces it to a zero row; contributes nothing, costs one reduction. No special handling. |\n| E7 | **Two senders in frame** | `streamId` lock (A9); packets from the unlocked stream are discarded and surfaced as `E-FOREIGN-STREAM`. |\n| E8 | **Tab backgrounded on the sender** | `rAF` stops in a background tab, so a 10-hour transfer silently halts. Wake Lock does **not** cover this. Detect via `visibilitychange` and warn loudly; the transfer is paused, not failed. |\n| E9 | **Camera permission revoked mid-run** | Pause, preserve the bitmap, prompt for re-grant. Never silently truncate. **The kept partial artefact follows T4b's deletion lifecycle** — warn the user before keeping it, provide a delete control, and reap on startup. |\n| E11 | **Abandoned staging file** | Sender-side staging keyed by `streamId`; on startup, reap staging files with no active session. This is the CRC-8 false-accept path (§7.1) and MUST be implemented — at GB scale a silent re-do costs hours. |\n| E13 | **Whole-file hash fails after all blocks pass** | Indicates E5 or a block-hash collision. Report `E-FILE-HASH`; keep the output and label it unverified rather than deleting hours of work. |\n| E14 | **Filename with path separators or control bytes** | Sanitise on export (§12, T2). Never write an attacker-chosen path. |\n| E15 | **Decompression fails at the end** | All blocks verified but the gzip stream is invalid → `E-DECOMPRESS`; keep the compressed artefact so nothing is lost. **The kept artefact follows T4b's deletion lifecycle** — warn the user before keeping it, provide a delete control, and reap on startup. |\n| E16 | **Worker crash mid-block** | Restart the worker, discard the active block only, keep the bitmap. |\n| E17a | **Sender-side thermal throttling** | Observed: the bench laptop decayed 6.7 → 2.4 fps over two minutes. Locally observable, so D18b's local step-down applies. |\n| E17b | **Receiver-side thermal throttling** | Observed at **70 °C / throttling threshold within 20–30 minutes**. Performance budgets and benchmark contract\n\n### 13.1 Budgets — committed, not forecast\n\n§15's table is *expectation*. These are the numbers the build is held to.\n\n**Throughput basis.** All throughput budgets are **user-visible file bytes per second** after:\n- Fountain coding overhead (+12% p99 at K=768 with D25's cap)\n- Erasure loss (20–30% assumed band per D18c)\n- Dwell overhead (60% standing overhead per §8.1)\n\nThe gross wire rate at the R2 nominal rung (v16-L, 2 packets/tile, 15 tiles, 15 fps) is\n**112.5 KB/s payload** (7.5 KB/frame × 15 fps). This is the **minimum viable duration** before R11's thermal throttling mitigation (duty-cycle reduction) must engage. The system is not required to avoid throttling indefinitely—only to (a) sustain long enough for practical use and (b) detect and surface throttling when it occurs (E17b, D27). | Phase 3; validated by T-long-run |\n| **Warn threshold** (D23) | estimated duration **> 30 min** → explicit confirm | Phase 4 |\n| **Refuse threshold** (D23) | estimated duration **> 24 h**, or quota insufficient → refuse with an override | Phase 4 |\n\n### 13.2 Benchmark denominator — the contract\n\nEvery throughput number in this repo MUST state all of these, or it is not a measurement:\n\n| Parameter | Reference value |\n|---|---|\n| **Unit** | **User-visible file bytes per second.** Not wire bytes.
